newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish utility signs five trillion lira accords.
newsitem.headline: Turkish utility signs five trillion lira accords.

text.p: Turkey's state electricity producer TEAS on Friday signed accords worth five trillion lira ($41.3 million) under its 1997 investment plan for transmission lines, transformer stations and underground power cables.
TEAS initialled an agreement in Ankara for the construction of two underground cables by Demirer Kablo and Turk Siemens, largely owned by German Siemens AG for 1.506 trillion lira.

An accord for the construction of 21 transformer stations having 154-380 kilovolt capacity was awarded to local companies Hayrettin Ozdil, Bogazici, AEG Genel and Usluer for a total 2.029 trillion lira.
The companies Mitas and Galkon were award a contract to build 16, 154-kilovolt transmission lines for a total 1.428 trillion lira.
TEAS managing director Afif Demirkiran told reporters at the signing ceremony that TEAS would meet the cost of the contracts through its own resources.
He said the projects would be realised in the latter part of 1997 and in 1998.
